beats.narration: Checkpoint five: four tasks, four configuration snippets, each labeled with an agent type and a cost lever. If you haven't matched them yet, pause here and do it first.

The single-fact lookup against a stable corpus takes C: fetch-once retrieval on the smallest model that works. No iteration, no fan-out, nothing extra to pay for. The broad research question that splits into independent parts is the one genuine home for A, orchestrator-worker — the fan-out multiplier finally buys parallel exploration. The user-facing request takes D, streaming: the reply feels instant because the first token arrives early. And the cost-sensitive, non-urgent job takes B: batches for roughly half the cost, caching for the context that recurs — latency is the one thing this job has to spare.

elements.code:
lookup       →  C  fetch-once + smallest model
research     →  A  orchestrator-worker
user-facing  →  D  streaming
non-urgent   →  B  batch + cache

elements.text: A fits ONLY where the work truly splits
batch jobs: latency is the currency you spend

beats.narration: The grading trick: the agent type and the lever are judged together, and the lever has to move the constraint that scenario actually has. Streaming a batch job moves nothing. Next: security.
